subject: NovusPay onboarding: concurrency acceptance & closure
messages:
From: James Li <james.li@novuspay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novuspay.com>, ops-eng@novuspay.com
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovusPay onboarding: concurrency acceptance & closure

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the run yesterday. Quick note from our side: our SREs still see CPU saturation at 80% when we push beyond 175 concurrent sessions for the payment-authorization flow. The latency P95 climbs above the target (we hit ~340ms P95 on the 1.6k token average). Can you confirm the final acceptance criteria you want us to sign off on?

We'd like a short summary we can hand to our procurement folks for closure (they need a clear statement: "passes throughput X with tail latency Y on the dedicated profile").

—James
James Li
Head of Platform, NovusPay

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: James Li <james.li@novuspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@novuspay.com>, ops-eng@novuspay.com
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovusPay onboarding: concurrency acceptance & closure

James — thanks for the data point and for looping in your SREs. Below is the concise acceptance summary we propose for procurement, plus the test artifacts we will attach: 

Acceptance summary (proposed):
- Workload: Payment-authorization conversational flow, average prompt+context ~1.6k tokens.
- Throughput: sustained 160 concurrent sessions with 95th-percentile per-response latency <= 300ms on Redwood Dedicated (g4dn-like profile).
- Tail target: 99th percentile per-response latency <= 550ms under sustained 160 concurrent sessions over a 30-minute window.
- Token-cost and error-rate: <0.3% generation error rate and average token egress cost as agreed in SOW.

Artifacts attached: consolidated run CSV (novus_concurrency_results_20250911.csv), final runbook (onboard-runbook-v2.pdf), and raw Grafana links in the Drive folder.

If those numbers look good, we can mark the onboarding benchmark as "Accepted" and issue the final onboarding acceptance note for procurement. If Novus wants to push to 180+ concurrency, we should scope a short follow-up optimization sprint (quantization tweaks + batching profile updates).

Next steps (quick):
1) Confirm acceptance summary by EOB today — James/Priya.
2) Redwood to provide single-paragraph certificate for procurement once confirmed.
3) If closing, schedule a 30-min wrap call to review billing impact and commit to a Dedicated pool size.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novuspay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, James Li <james.li@novuspay.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovusPay onboarding: concurrency acceptance & closure

Thanks — that proposed summary looks aligned with procurement needs. Couple clarifying asks from procurement / legal:
- Can Redwood confirm if the 99th percentile is computed per-response or per-session? (they prefer "per-response" for compliance).
- Please include the exact dataset and test window used for the CSV (start/end timestamps) so audit can match run artifacts to the acceptance note.

If you can provide those two items we'll be able to sign off and route to procurement by tomorrow.

Best,
Priya
VP, Engineering Operations, NovusPay

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novuspay.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, James Li <james.li@novuspay.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovusPay onboarding: concurrency acceptance & closure

Priya — good questions. Quick answers and the audit fields we added to the CSV: 

- Metric definition: 99th percentile is computed per-response (each model completion response). We'll state that explicitly in the acceptance note.
- Run window and dataset: the attached CSV includes columns: run_id, start_ts, end_ts, concurrent_sessions, avg_tokens, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, error_rate, cpu_util. The run we flagged as the canonical acceptance run is run_id=run-9843-final (start_ts=2025-09-11T02:00:00Z, end_ts=2025-09-11T02:30:00Z).

Brief observation on the 175->saturation point James mentioned: during the run we saw queue length growth at the request router after ~170 concurrent sessions due to client burst patterns; average per-request processing remained stable with KV cache hit rate > 94%. That suggests we can gain ~10% headroom by smoothing client side bursts or by enabling the "aggressive batch" profile. If Novus wants we can run the two-minute burst-resilience sweep next week (low-effort).

I've attached the CSV and runbook; see Drive folder for Grafana snapshots.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Engineering Programs, Redwood Inference

From: James Li <james.li@novuspay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novuspay.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovusPay onboarding: concurrency acceptance & closure

Thanks — that addresses procurement's questions. We reviewed run-9843-final and procurement is comfortable with the per-response 99p and the run window. We're ready to accept the benchmark as long as Redwood provides the one-paragraph acceptance note and confirms the recommended mitigations won't change committed cost estimates (we don't want surprise billing).

Can you send the acceptance note and confirm cost neutrality for the smoothing/batching recommendations? If both are positive we'll close and route through procurement.

—James
James Li
Head of Platform, NovusPay
